blocks.text: Setting up Google Sheets for media planners on Mac

Google Sheets does not have a native Mac app. You work inside a browser. Chrome is the most reliable choice for this. To make Sheets feel like a desktop app, create a Progressive Web App shortcut. Open sheets.google.com in Chrome, click the three-dot menu, select Cast, Save, and Share, then click Install page as app. This puts a dedicated icon in your Dock.
Why media planners struggle with spreadsheets

You juggle reach, frequency, and budget data daily. When you have multiple tabs open and large datasets, performance can lag. The limit of 20 million cells is generous, but large sheets slow down when many people edit them at once. If you hit a wall, check your formulas for circular references.
Essential keyboard shortcuts for your Mac

items: Find and replace text using ⌘ + ⇧ + H.
Use Option + / to open the tool finder search bar.

blocks.text: Media planners spend roughly 28 percent of their week on email. You often copy data from a sheet into an email draft. Hold fn to dictate your analysis directly into your email client. This saves you from switching windows and losing your place in the data.

Lazur lives in your Mac notch. When you are stuck, hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask where a specific setting is. Lazur will draw a circle on your screen to show you the button. If you need to know how to perform a complex calculation, ask Lazur to guide you. It will wait for you to click each step in the menu.

When you have thousands of rows, manual sorting takes time. Use the Data menu to create filters. If you need to clean your data, use the split text feature to separate campaign names from IDs. Always keep a backup of your original data in a hidden tab before you run large find and replace jobs.
Common mistakes in media planning sheets

items: Hardcoding values instead of using cell references.
Forgetting to freeze the top row, making it hard to track headers.
Over-merging cells which breaks sorting and filtering.
Ignoring the revision history when multiple people share the file.
Using too many complex array formulas that slow down the sheet.

blocks.text: If your sheet feels slow, check the number of active collaborators. If more than 15 people are in the file, it will lag. Ask team members to close tabs they are not actively using.
blocks.title: Performance tip

blocks.text: Use conditional formatting to highlight performance metrics that fall below your target. This gives you a visual alert as soon as you open the sheet. You can also use dropdown lists to standardize campaign status tracking across your team. This prevents typos and keeps your data clean for future reporting.

Your spreadsheet is just one part of your day. Use Apple Calendar for time-blocking your data analysis sessions. If you use NotePlan or Things 3, keep your campaign notes there rather than in the sheet. This keeps your spreadsheet focused on numbers and your project management focused on tasks.
How to get help with Lazur

Lazur is not a plugin. It does not edit your cells or click buttons for you. It is a voice assistant that helps you find your way. If you forget where the pivot table tool is, just ask. It will point it out. It is a tool for your Mac that helps you work faster.

faq.question: Does Lazur work inside Google Sheets?
faq.answer: Lazur works on your Mac screen. It can see your Google Sheets window, point at buttons, and guide you through menus, but it cannot edit your data directly.

faq.question: Is there a native Mac app for Google Sheets?
faq.answer: No. Google Sheets is a web app. You can create a desktop shortcut using Chrome to make it open in its own window.

faq.question: How do I speed up a slow spreadsheet?
faq.answer: Reduce the number of active collaborators, remove unnecessary formulas, and delete unused rows or columns. Avoid having too many complex functions like VLOOKUP in every cell.

faq.question: Can Lazur draft my media plan emails?
faq.answer: Yes. Hold fn to dictate your text directly into your email app. Lazur will format your speech into clean, professional text.
